description:
Issue summary:
BrightQuery reports a gradual throughput degradation on their dedicated GPU pool during a staged model rollout window overnight. Degradation presents as progressive slot evaporation (fewer available GPU slots reported by allocator) over ~30 minutes, followed by partial recovery after an autoscaler rebalance.

Impact:
- Affected customer experienced increased p95/p99 latency and dropped concurrency for ~30 minutes in us-west region during rollout (customer traffic window: 02:00–03:00 UTC).
- Errors were mainly 429s and occasional 5xxs as requests hit capacity fallback.

Environment:
- Deployment: Dedicated (reserved) pool, us-west
- Customer tier: dedicated
- Models: redwood-open-13B (primary), rw-embed-2B (background batch)
- Time window: 2026-03-13 02:15–03:00 UTC

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Start a staged rollout that gradually shifts 20%→60% traffic to a new model variant over 20 minutes.
2) Observe allocator slot counts and autoscaler decisions.
3) Monitor p95/p99 latency and error rates.

Observed behavior:
- Progressive decline in reported free GPU slots in the reserved pool (allocator metric allocator.free_slots shows stepwise drop).
- Autoscaler triggers a scale-up but allocation lag and prefetch contention prevent immediate recovery; customers see elevated p99 latencies until rebalance completes.
- Sidecar/prefetcher logs show repeated short prefetch bursts coinciding with new variant rollout traffic.

Expected behavior:
- Pool should absorb staged rollout without slot evaporation by prioritizing active inference allocations and smooth prefetch coordination.

Relevant logs/metrics/snapshots:
- Allocator dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/allocators/reserved-us-west?panel=free_slots
- Trace of the event window: https://tracing.redwood/trace/evt-20260313-uw1-88a3
- Customer-provided client logs attached as snippets in comments.

Additional context:
- Customer was performing a canary-style model swap; background embedding batch jobs were scheduled in adjacent timeslot in same pool (rw-embed-2B).
- Pool has autoscale cooldown set to 90s and reserved burst credits remaining ~120% of baseline at time of event.
comments: 2026-03-13 09:21 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer opened ticket; included client side latency graphs and a flame graph of request distribution. Customer notes this only started after they initiated their staged rollout. Asked for urgent triage due to SLAs.

2026-03-13 09:45 - Ravi Patel (SRE): Initial triage: allocator shows free_slots decline starting at 02:12 UTC with matching increase in allocator.waiting_allocations. Prefetcher logs show bursty prefetch calls from customer sidecar ~02:10–02:25 UTC. Kicking off deeper investigation and attaching Grafana snapshots.

2026-03-13 11:03 - Elena Gomez (Platform Eng): Hypothesis: prefetch bursts are monopolizing ephemeral slot reservations causing allocator to mark slots as transiently unavailable (slot evaporation). Also saw affinity hints from staged rollout creating small gang scheduling delays. Reproducing on staging with synthetic canary workload.

2026-03-13 13:50 - BrightQuery (Customer): Confirmed they had an embedding batch scheduled to start at 02:05 UTC; they will reschedule to avoid overlap while we investigate. Asked for recommended immediate mitigation to reduce impact tonight.

2026-03-13 15:12 - Ravi Patel (SRE): Temporary mitigation suggested: reduce prefetcher concurrency to 2 and set rollout ramp slower (10% increments with 120s waits). Customer applied change for tonight's rollout; reported partial improvement but still saw a short slot dip at 02:22 UTC. Collecting further traces.

2026-03-14 07:30 - Platform Eng (Elena Gomez): Staging repro shows coordination issue between prefetcher and allocator where prefetch reservations are not being reclaimed fast enough when rollout changes affinity. Crafting a fix to prioritize active inference allocations over prefetch reservations and add a short TTL on ephemeral prefetch slots.

2026-03-14 10:02 - Ravi Patel (SRE): Rolling a canary patch to allocator: prioritize permanent inference allocations and lower prefetch reservation TTL from 30s->8s in canary ring. Monitoring canary metrics for slot churn and p99 latency.

2026-03-14 11:45 - BrightQuery (Customer): Noted that since canary patch applied to portion of us-west pool, their p99 latency returned to baseline in the canary zone. They request a full rollout and post-deployment verification runbook.
investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
1) Root cause appears to be coordination mismatch: prefetcher was creating short-lived ephemeral reservations which were not reclaimed quickly when staged rollout shifted traffic; allocator considered them live, reducing free_slots (slot evaporation).
2) Gang/affinity hints from staged variant caused a small increase in allocation latency (waiting_allocations), amplifying the visible impact.
3) Background embedding batch scheduled by customer at same time increased IO and prefetch pressure.
Evidence:
- allocator.free_slots and allocator.waiting_allocations time series show correlated drops and spikes.
- Prefetcher logs have multiple concurrent prefetch workers firing in 02:10–02:25 UTC window.
- Staging repro confirms lowering prefetch concurrency and TTL prevents evaporation.
resolution_notes:
Workarounds and next steps:
- Immediate workaround used by customer: slow rollout ramp (10% every 120s) and reduce prefetcher concurrency; reschedule heavy embedding batch away from rollout windows. This reduced amplitude of slot evaporation.
- Short-term fix (canary deployed 2026-03-14): allocator change to deprioritize ephemeral prefetch reservations and TTL reduced to 8s. Canary improved slot stability and p99 latency in affected zone.
- Medium-term actions: merge allocator change and prefetcher coordination PRs, add explicit prefetch reservation metrics and an alarm on ephemeral_slot_ratio > 0.15, update dedicated runbook with guidance on scheduling background batch jobs during rollouts.
- Follow-up: full rollout of allocator change after 24h canary observation, customer acceptance test planned for 2026-03-16.
